gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak stands tall, its lowercase rising like a stubby carpenter's pencil. Azonix sits above it in thin, uniform strokes, so a long page moves from commanding headline to a body that reads open and unhurried.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Azonix looks like letters bent from a single wire, authoritative and wide. Noto Sans Bengali follows with distinctly open mouths and capitals barely above its lowercase, so the heading holds the eye and the text underneath lets it rest.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Azonix draws every letter with a monoweight stroke, wide and commanding, with capitals barely above its lowercase. But shrink that heading and the words take a moment to knit together, while Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, with its tightly coiled lowercase, stays easy to read.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi reads contemporary, with a high mean line and curves left open at the ends. Azonix is the one to lean on for a gentle, uniform-lined shout, while the sans-serif text gets on with the quieter work of being read.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Modern and a touch austere, Azonix lays down strokes like fine rope in wide, crisp capitals. And Noto Sans Buginese settles beneath it with open letter mouths like unjoined chalk arcs and short ascenders, giving the headline room to dominate.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Wire-bent letters up top, airy curves below. Shrink Azonix and its tubular forms start to need a moment to knit together, whereas Noto Sans Buhid keeps generous gaps between curve ends and stems at any size.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads clean, with terminals that stay apart like open scissor blades. Azonix brings a single line weight and wide, commanding capitals above it, and the tiny gaps under the ascender tops keep the text below quietly precise.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Noto Sans Chakma packs its lowercase up toward the capitals and leaves the s and c uncrowded and open. Azonix, pipe-cleaner thin, is the commanding half.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cham: Wide, wiry and sure of itself, Azonix holds one steady pen pressure from first letter to last. Noto Sans Cham follows with tall, rounded lowercase and open entries on its c shapes, and the heading is best given a generous size.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Wide, uniform strokes with real authority. Azonix gives no variation between thick and thin and commands attention, while Noto Sans Cherokee does the approachable work, with a tall band of letters and an e that keeps a wide gap at its terminal.
